around.headline: On-duty police officer's house burgled in Bengaluru
around.summary: A Bengaluru police officer's home was burgled while he was away on duty, per The Times of India. It's a reminder that even homes with an obvious connection to law enforcement aren't immune — a monitored alarm, visible CCTV, or a trusted neighbour keeping an eye out matters more than who lives there.

around.headline: Airport Metro (Blue Line) hits 72% work — but delays persist
around.summary: The 58-km Blue Line connecting the airport is now 72% complete, with reports detailing which stretches are on track and what's causing hold-ups elsewhere on the corridor, per The Times of India. If you're planning around a metro-to-airport commute, don't bank on the full line opening on the earliest floated date.

around.headline: Bengaluru's waste-collection overhaul promises more capacity — pourakarmikas say they were left out
around.summary: A revamped waste-management plan aims to boost collection capacity and citizen participation, but sanitation workers (pourakarmikas) say they were excluded from a key GBA planning meeting, per ThePrint and Bangalore Mirror. Worth watching whether your ward's collection timing or segregation rules change as the plan rolls out.

around.headline: Cauvery row escalates: Karnataka says it'll release water 'only if available'
around.summary: Karnataka's CM said Cauvery water releases to Tamil Nadu depend on availability as TN flags a 20 TMC deficit, while a Congress MLA quit over the state's drought-relief list, per The Times of India. Prolonged water-sharing disputes like this have historically preceded municipal supply tightening in the months that follow.

around.headline: Markets slide sharply — Sensex down 1,247 points
around.summary: Indian markets fell over 1.6% today, with the Sensex losing 1,247 points and the Nifty closing at 23,063, driven by a spike in crude oil prices and rising US bond yields, per BusinessLine. If you run SIPs, a single volatile session like this is routine noise, not a reason to change your plan.

around.headline: CJP threatens 'Jantar Mantar 2.0' protest if Election Commission chief doesn't resign
around.summary: The Campaign for Judicial Accountability and Reforms has threatened a fresh round of protests unless CEC Gyanesh Kumar resigns, amid ongoing controversy over the electoral-roll revision (SIR) that earlier flagged disproportionate deletions in Bengaluru itself, per The Hindu. If you haven't checked the draft roll for your own booth yet, this is a good week to do it before any correction window narrows further.

street_smart.title: At a weekend market stall, a vendor is selling loose, unbranded pickle jars — no label, no manufacturer name, no FSSAI number — for half the price of the packaged brands next to them. He tells you it's 'homemade, all-natural, no preservatives.' It looks and smells fine. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: The Hindu, Sept 24 — a pickle manufacturing unit in Bengaluru was sealed today over unhygienic conditions. This unlicensed/unhygienic-food-purchase mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart topic in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: You eat a lot of pickle at home and the price is tempting. The stall's been there for a few weekends and other shoppers are buying without a second thought.

choices.text: Buy a few jars right away — it's homemade and looks fresh, and homemade usually beats mass-produced anyway.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. 'Homemade' and 'looks fine' tell you nothing about hygiene — exactly what today's sealed Bengaluru pickle unit was accused of. Improperly processed or stored pickles can carry mould, botulism-causing bacteria, or contamination that isn't visible or detectable by smell, and without an FSSAI number there's no traceability if you fall sick.

choices.text: Ask to see an FSSAI registration/licence number, check for a batch or packing date, and skip the purchase if the seller can't show either.
choices.feedback: Correct. An FSSAI number (even the basic 14-digit registration for small vendors) means the seller is on record and can be traced and held accountable. No number, no batch/date marking — no purchase, regardless of how fresh it looks.

choices.text: Buy one small jar to taste-test first, and decide about the rest based on how it tastes.
choices.feedback: Risky. Taste won't catch what actually makes unhygienic food dangerous — bacterial or fungal contamination often shows no off-taste until well after it's made you ill, sometimes hours or days later. A taste test checks flavour, not safety.

choices.text: Skip buying, but don't bother reporting it since it's just one small stall.
choices.feedback: Risky. Not buying protects you, but an unreported unlicensed stall keeps selling to everyone else. A quick report to the local FSSAI office or BBMP health department (or via the FSSAI's consumer helpline) is what actually gets it inspected.

takeaways: Before buying any loose, unbranded packaged food — pickles, papads, sweets, spice mixes — check for a visible FSSAI registration/licence number; sellers are legally required to display one.
Taste and appearance don't reveal biological contamination — it's not a reliable safety check, however fresh something seems.
Report unlicensed or visibly unhygienic food sellers to FSSAI (foodlicensing.fssai.gov.in has a complaint option) or your local BBMP health office rather than just avoiding them yourself.

quiz.question: Per today's report, how far along is construction on Bengaluru's 58-km airport Metro (Blue Line)?
quiz.why: The Blue Line will link the airport to the city centre once finished; reports today pointed to right-of-way and utility-shifting issues as key causes of delay on parts of the corridor.

quiz.question: How many points did the Sensex lose in today's sharp market fall?
quiz.why: The fall was driven by a spike in crude oil prices and rising US bond yields — global cues that often ripple into Indian markets on the same trading day.

quiz.question: In today's Cauvery water-sharing row, what deficit did Tamil Nadu say it's facing?
quiz.why: TMC (thousand million cubic feet) is the standard unit used to measure river-water allocations between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu under Cauvery tribunal and Supreme Court orders.

quiz.question: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
quiz.why: Gujarat's coastline stretches over 1,600 km along the Arabian Sea — the longest of any Indian state, followed by Andhra Pradesh.

quiz.question: What is the 'repo rate' set by India's central bank, the RBI?
options: The interest rate at which RBI lends short-term funds to commercial banks
The tax rate on repossessed property
The exchange rate between the rupee and the dollar
The minimum wage rate for RBI employees
quiz.why: When the RBI cuts the repo rate, banks typically pass on lower loan interest rates to consumers, and raise them when it's hiked — it's the RBI's main lever for controlling inflation and growth.
